blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: In Example 1 of 9.1 we noticed that the remainder on dividing by \(x - 2\) was the same as the value of the dividend at \(x = 2\). The remainder theorem says this always happens when the divisor has the form \(x - a\). So the remainder can be found by one substitution, without any long division.
If a polynomial \(f(x)\) of degree \(n \ge 1\) is divided by \(x - a\) till no \(x\)-term exists in the remainder, then \(f(a)\) is the remainder.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
1. "Till no \(x\)-term exists in the remainder" means we divide until the remainder is a constant. With a divisor of degree 1 the remainder always has degree 0.
2. Read \(a\) carefully from the divisor: \(x - 3\) gives \(a = 3\); \(x + 1 = x - (-1)\) gives \(a = -1\). In general the remainder on dividing by \(x + a\) is \(f(-a)\).
3. A quick way to find \(a\): it is the value of \(x\) that makes the divisor zero.
Suppose we divide a polynomial \(f(x)\) by \((x - a)\). Then there exists a unique quotient \(q(x)\) and a unique remainder \(R\) such that

Substituting \(x = a\) in equation (i), we get
\(f(x) = (a - a)q(a) + R\)
\[f(a) = R\]
Hence remainder \(= f(a)\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the proof the book prints \(f(x) = (a - a)q(a) + R\). After substituting \(x = a\) the left side is also evaluated at \(a\); the line should read \(f(a) = (a - a)q(a) + R\). The next line, \(f(a) = R\), is correct.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Why the proof works: at \(x = a\) the factor \(x - a\) becomes \(a - a = 0\), and zero times anything is zero, so the whole first term \((x - a)q(x)\) disappears. Only \(R\) is left. \(R\) does not change with \(x\) because it is a constant (the divisor has degree 1).

blocks.title: Example 3
blocks.problem: Find the remainder when \(f(x) = x^{4} + x^{3} + x^{2} + 1\) is divided by \(x + 1\) without performing division.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{4} + x^{3} + x^{2} + 1\), divisor \(x + 1\).
To find: the remainder, without dividing.
Method: remainder theorem. Write the divisor as \(x - a\), then the remainder is \(f(a)\).

Step 1: Find \(a\)
\[x - a = x + 1\]
\[\Rightarrow a = -1\]
Why: \(x + 1 = x - (-1)\), so \(a\) is \(-1\), the value of \(x\) that makes the divisor zero.

Step 2: Evaluate \(f(-1)\)
\[\text{Remainder} = f(-1)\]
\[= (-1)^{4} + (-1)^{3} + (-1)^{2} + 1\]
\[= 1 + (-1) + 1 + 1 = 2\]
Why: by the remainder theorem. An even power of \(-1\) is \(1\) and an odd power is \(-1\).

Check:
Long division gives the quotient \(x^{3} + x - 1\), and
\[(x + 1)(x^{3} + x - 1)\]
\[= x^{4} + x^{3} + x^{2} - 1\]
Adding the remainder 2 gives \(x^{4} + x^{3} + x^{2} + 1 = f(x)\).

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: Find the value of \(k\) if the polynomial \(x^{3} + kx^{2} - 7x + 6\) has a remainder \(-4\), when divided by \(x + 2\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{3} + kx^{2} - 7x + 6\), divisor \(x + 2\), remainder \(-4\).
To find: the value of \(k\).
Method: by the remainder theorem the remainder is \(f(-2)\). Its value contains \(k\); setting it equal to \(-4\) gives an equation for \(k\).

Step 1: Find \(a\)
\[x - a = x + 2\]
\[\Rightarrow a = -2\]
Why: \(x + 2 = x - (-2)\).

Step 2: Find the remainder in terms of \(k\)
\[\text{Remainder} = f(-2)\]
\[= (-2)^{3} + k(-2)^{2} - 7(-2) + 6\]
\[= -8 + 4k + 14 + 6\]
\[= 4k + 12\]
The book labels this line "Remember \(= f(-2)\)"; it means Remainder (see the Book correction below).
Why: \((-2)^{3} = -8\), \((-2)^{2} = 4\) and \(-7(-2) = +14\).

Step 3: Use the given remainder
\[4k + 12 = -4\]
\[\Rightarrow 4k = -16\]
\[\Rightarrow k = -4\]
Why: the remainder is given as \(-4\); subtract 12 from both sides, then divide by 4.

Check:
With \(k = -4\), \(f(x) = x^{3} - 4x^{2} - 7x + 6\) and
\[f(-2) = -8 - 16 + 14 + 6 = -4\]
which is the given remainder.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the solution of Example 4 the book writes "Remember \(= f(-2)\)". The word should be "Remainder": Remainder \(= f(-2)\) by the remainder theorem.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Remainder theorem: when \(f(x)\) is divided by \(x - a\), the remainder is \(f(a)\).
2. \(a\) is the value of \(x\) that makes the divisor zero: for \(x + 2\), \(a = -2\).
3. The remainder theorem finds only the remainder, not the quotient.
4. If the remainder is given and \(f(x)\) has an unknown, write \(f(a) =\) given remainder and solve.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.text:
1. Taking the wrong sign for \(a\): for \(x + 1\) use \(f(-1)\), not \(f(1)\).
2. Losing signs with powers of negative numbers: \((-2)^{3} = -8\) but \((-2)^{2} = +4\).
3. Forgetting to put brackets round the negative number when substituting: write \(k(-2)^{2}\), not \(k - 2^{2}\).
